approved_scope.title: Reuse a cached validation snapshot or read-cache verdict only in the build that wrote it, so a stale pass cannot hide a new refusal (#878)
approved_scope.description: Reuse a cached validation snapshot or read-cache verdict only in the build that wrote it, so a stale pass cannot hide a new refusal (#878)
acceptance_criteria: A validation snapshot recorded by any other build, including one that reports the same package version and one written before #878, is not replayed: a default specsync check re-validates the spec and reports the refusal this build makes (a duplicated requirement ID in the #878 case), while a snapshot recorded by this build still replays.

Both bindings come from one build fingerprint compiled in by build.rs over src/, Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock and build.rs; dropping it from either digest fails a test (mutation), and the end-to-end repro (released 6.2.0 then this build) reports the duplicate instead of All specs unchanged.
The persistent read cache written by another build of the same version, such as a sibling worktree sharing the Git common directory, is not loaded; its passing verdicts are recomputed live.

answers.constraints: SPEED-1.c: a cache keyed by content digest needs a correct invalidation rule, and a build that judges differently must never reuse another build's result; specs/change/change.3md: a stale pass must not stand as the answer; the 95% plan: failing test first, never weaken a test, gate or bound; Leif chose approach B (build fingerprint) over an explicit rules-version constant
